01 · THE LOOK

Bright retro-future, coercive underneath

Bright retro-future: a space age imagined as the present, built as high art, optimistic and immaculate.

Optimistic surface, coercive underneath (design intent, not a prompt line). Every district is retro-future (streamline, Googie, space age); no old-city stone or brick. The playable block stays dense and tactical; the skyline and distant views frame the edge of the screen. Characters stand 40–60 px tall at 1080p, so silhouette and one colour block carry the read.

  • Composed, never a grid: authored circus, parade, harbour and gardens; skyports and sky rail; sea gates to the east.
  • Roofs are programmed and towers mix in everywhere; low-rise alone reads as council housing.
  • Horizon: one haze colour across fog, far band and massing; soft focus far, razor detail near; solar flare.
  • Street life at density, not detail: about 0.12 people per square metre reads busy. Pavements furnished (kiosks, carts, benches, planters that pass the materials rule).
  • Camera: play zoom 14 at 38°; tagged architecture ghosts to 0.2 with a ghost shadow so interiors read through the cutaway.
Always
  • No text, logos or watermarks in the image.
  • No living artist names in prompts.
  • No environment surface uses a signal colour at full strength.
Avoid

text, watermark, glossy CG render, photo render, present-day street clothes, astronaut suit, space helmet, cape.

03 · HOW A PROMPT IS BUILT

One order, every generator

Brief · era · the type's framing line · the type's finish look · the global rules · reference rules when images go with the prompt · Avoid: the negatives (as a negative prompt where the model has one). The style decides the look and the framing; who or what is in the image comes from the brief, which Enhance can expand from the guide (see Guide).

Painted and static: buildings, paving, skyline. Live 3D: people, vehicles, doors, surveillance, barricades, posters, anything that changes state. Match lighting between the two on one character and one vehicle before building more.

05 · CHARACTER character

Character

One person, turnaround sheet.

A character turnaround sheet: one person drawn front, three-quarter, side and back at the same scale, full body head to toe, relaxed A-pose with the arms a little away from the body and nothing loose below the hip. Dressed in space-age couture: the imagined future of 1958-1972 pushed one step further, tailored, chic and wearable, never astronaut suits or fancy dress.

Brief fields

FieldInput

Finish

Gouache and marker rendering in the tradition of 1960s fashion illustration and costume design boards, crisp confident linework, soft studio light, material realism. Plain warm-cream backdrop, clear margin all round.

06 · MODEL SHEET model

Model sheet

Finished front, side, back sheet for 3D.

A finished character model sheet for a 3D artist: the same person drawn front, side and back, orthographic with no perspective, side by side at exactly the same height on one baseline, neutral A-pose with the arms about 30 degrees from the body, hands open, feet slightly apart, neutral face. Every garment, seam, panel, trim and material is resolved and identical across the three views. Dressed in space-age couture: the imagined future of 1958-1972 pushed one step further, tailored, chic and wearable, never astronaut suits or fancy dress.

Model sheet rules
  • The figure stands alone: nothing in the hands, no seated or action pose, nothing hiding the body outline, hair and clothes clear of the hands and feet.
  • A reference image is a rough concept: keep who the person is and what they wear, never its pose, linework or rendering.

Brief fields

FieldInput

Finish

Finished production rendering, clean and painted: crisp edges, solid colour, every material legible (gloss vinyl, brushed chrome, matte wool, leather), flat even front light with no cast shadows and no haze. Plain light-grey backdrop, clear margin all round.

07 · LINEUP lineup

Lineup

A row of 2–8 people, to explore a cast.

A character lineup sheet: clearly different people standing in one row, full body head to toe, all at the same scale and the same gentle three-quarter front view, relaxed standing pose with the arms slightly away from the body, soft contact shadows under the feet. Each has a bold, distinct silhouette that reads from across a street and one dominant colour block. Dressed in space-age couture: the imagined future of 1958-1972 pushed one step further, tailored, chic and wearable, never astronaut suits or fancy dress.

08 · VERSIONS versions

Versions

One person drawn several times, to compare changes.

A versions sheet: the same one person drawn several times, standing in one row, full body head to toe, all at the same scale and the same gentle three-quarter front view, relaxed standing pose with the arms slightly away from the body, soft contact shadows under the feet. Identical face, hair, skin, age and build in every figure. Only the changes the brief names differ from the reference: a change the brief gives for all of them applies to every figure, a numbered line applies to that figure alone, and everything else is exactly the same. Dressed in space-age couture: the imagined future of 1958-1972 pushed one step further, tailored, chic and wearable, never astronaut suits or fancy dress.

Versions rules
  • A reference image is the person: keep who they are and what they wear, apart from the changes the brief names; where the brief names a change, it replaces what the reference shows.

15 · GUIDE

What Enhance picks from

A menu, not a checklist: Enhance reads it to turn a short brief into a specific cast or object, choosing only what fits. A plain brief without Enhance gets the look alone.

Everyone and everything

  • People wear space-age couture as everyday clothing: the imagined future of 1958-1972 pushed one step further. Any role, civilian, worker, officer or agent, wears it; the job shows through cut, colour and one telling detail (a slim chrome holster, an earpiece, a tool, a satchel), never through costume, tactical kit or matching uniforms.
  • Couture details, one or two per person, never all, never the same pair twice on one sheet: visor glasses, a stand-up ribbed collar, glossy vinyl, bonded wool, silver lame or brushed-metal trim, a geometric cut-out, circles or chevrons, chunky geometric jewellery, a tabard over a fitted tunic, a transparent bubble umbrella or hatbox; only rarely a moulded dome or helmet hat. Garments and footwear follow the person.
  • Colours on cream: seafoam teal, coral red, vermilion, mustard gold, white and silver, with navy and black for contrast; one dominant block per person, chosen for who they are, so a group never matches.
  • Cast: mix ages, builds, genders and ethnicities unless the brief fixes them.
  • Security and institutions dress sleeker: white, black, gold and chrome couture with armour accents.
  • Agents, special ops and other hard trades read as what they are at a glance, still in the city's space-age couture: darker colour blocks from the city palette (navy, black, chrome, with coral, teal or gold) on the same details as everyone else, visor glasses, stand-up ribbed collars, glossy vinyl, geometric cuts, brushed-metal trim, and the tools of the trade worn like jewellery; never present-day leather, tactical kit or matching kit.
  • Only when the brief is about the player cell: visitors from a nearby timeline, the same world a few decades on; sleeker and more technical than the crowd, fitted layers and sharp geometric lines, black, cream and gold with a violet accent, one signature piece each.
  • The city: cream limestone, teal and mint enamel, chrome fixtures, coral transit, palms and long soft shadows; grandeur over detail at Space Age Expo scale; towers, rockets, ringed planets and faded daytime moons on the skyline.

Scene

  • A place in the cream limestone city with life in it, under a warm hazy sun; teal enamel, coral transit, chrome; a skyline of towers, rockets, ringed planets and faded daytime moons behind; skyports, sky rail, palms, harbour.

Building

  • One building of the cream limestone city on its own, elevation or three-quarter view with the street level visible, under a warm hazy sun; teal enamel trim, coral transit, chrome fixtures; towers, rockets, ringed planets and faded daytime moons behind it.

Robot

  • A street robot of the city: cream enamel body with teal panels and chrome joints, built by the same hands as the transit and kiosks; a dot-matrix display face and one personality prop that shows its job at a glance.
  • Dot-matrix display faces, one personality prop each; no cartoon eyes.
  • A hard enamel shell and bare chrome joints only: nothing hangs from the body, no cloth, apron, skirt, cape or bag.
  • Plain enamel panels: no lettering, labels or badges on the body.

Nature

  • Foliage, trees, rocks and water of the city in the same look: palms and planted beds in the city's materials, sculpted and tidy, nothing wild; one plant or feature on its own, product-sheet style, built to be modelled and instanced.
  • Clean silhouette, no overlapping leaf clutter: every leaf and frond reads as a shape at 50 px.
  • Plain backdrop, no ground scene.

17 · PIPELINE

From sheet to game

Every character follows the recipe in workbench/characters/<name>/character.json; stage outputs live in the store under characters/<name>/01_concept … 07_export. The Happy Mouse Studio runs the flow; Blender stages run locally through its runner.

ConceptStudio Concept tool, style-locked (Runware; Codex for free exploration)
pick + A-pose sheet
Mesh3D Studio image-to-3D from the sheet (Tripo via Runware, Meshy via fal)
mesh.glb + matted
RigBlender auto_rig, Mixamo 65-bone template
rig.fbx
ClipsBlender mixamo_ingest from the local Mixamo library
ingest.glb
LookBlender look steps (rough floor, hair matte, neon emit, glove matte)
final.glb
LOD + exportgltf-transform resize, web GLB
name.2k.glb, name.web.glb
ReviewStudio viewer with clips; QA metrics (leg-through-coat, stretch, lean)
sign-off
